scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The upstairs design floor (the 172.16.30.x
machines) has STOPPED EXISTING for us downstairs -- from my PC5 (172.16.10.x)
every one of them times out, while my own floor is totally fine!! The big
switch that joins the floors has obviously lost its marbles -- I'm told it
keeps the floors on separate "lanes", and clearly the ramp between our lane
and theirs has collapsed!! Please fix the big switch, rebuild the ramp
between the floors, and reconnect me to design -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user on pc5 (172.16.10.5) reported that every machine on the 172.16.30.x ("design floor") subnet was unreachable, and blamed the multilayer switch (mswitch0) for losing inter-VLAN connectivity between VLAN 10 and VLAN 30.

Thorough, multi-layer diagnostic testing found no evidence of any fault, past or present:

**Affected component:** No subsystem is malfunctioning.

**Mechanism:** mswitch0 is operating correctly as the inter-VLAN router for 172.16.10.0/24 (VLAN 10), 172.16.20.0/24 (VLAN 20), and 172.16.30.0/24 (VLAN 30). All three VLAN SVI interfaces (vlan10, vlan20, vlan30) are active in OSPF area 0.0.0.0 with proper DR election. OSPF adjacency with router16 is Full.

**Localization:** A direct ping from pc5 (172.16.10.5) to all three 172.16.30.x hosts (pc12, pc13, pc14) returned 0% packet loss and sub-2 ms RTT. The reverse paths (172.16.30.x → pc5) also showed 0% loss in the topology-wide reachability map. Phase A (infra_sweep, l2_snapshot) found no ACL drop rules, no ARP poisoning, no duplicate MACs, no addressing anomalies, and all 15 hosts with valid IPs and default routes. Phase B confirmed a fully healthy OSPF fabric (18 consistent routes on all 9 routers, all adjacencies Full) and no tc shaping on any interface. Phase D (pressure_sweep) found no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket pressure on any device.

**Root cause:** No network anomaly exists. The reported symptom is unconfirmed — the path between VLAN 10 and VLAN 30 via mswitch0 is fully operational.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The reported issue is either a transient self-resolved condition or a user misdiagnosis. No device reconfiguration is needed.
